definitions.explanation: Having an extremely sharp or refined ability to perceive, detect, or respond. Used for senses, intuition, or mental acuity.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{鋭敏|えいびん}な{感覚|かんかく}の{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}だ。
examples.english: She has a keen sense of perception.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}は{人間|にんげん}よりはるかに{鋭敏|えいびん}な{嗅覚|きゅうかく}を{持|も}つ。
examples.english: Dogs have a far more acute sense of smell than humans.

examples.japanese: {時代|じだい}の{変化|へんか}に{鋭敏|えいびん}に{反応|はんのう}できる{企業|きぎょう}だけが{生|い}き{残|のこ}る。
examples.english: Only companies that can respond keenly to changes in the times will survive.

notes:
USAGE:
Describes heightened sensitivity or sharpness of perception, whether physical senses or mental awareness. More formal and literary than {鋭|するど}い (sharp).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {鋭敏|えいびん}: keen, acute (formal, emphasizes refined sensitivity)
- {鋭|するど}い: sharp (general, everyday usage)
- {敏感|びんかん}: sensitive (reactive to stimuli, sometimes overly so)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鋭敏|えいびん}な{感覚|かんかく} (keen sense)
- {鋭敏|えいびん}な{嗅覚|きゅうかく} (acute sense of smell)
- {鋭敏|えいびん}に{反応|はんのう}する (to react keenly)
